HPV: catch-up through age 18 for those not adequately vaccinated is not encoded as a separate rule; only a by-age-13 completion check was created (derived age, needs human review).

HPV: 2- vs 3-dose series depends on age at initial vaccination (9-14 vs 15+); grammar cannot express birth-relative dose timing. For the age-13 cohort initiation is necessarily before 15, so 2 doses suffice unless immunocompromised/HIV (3 doses). A child starting at 12 may not finish by end of the year turning 13 (6-12 month interval).

HPV: minimum intervals (5 months for 2-dose; 4 weeks/12 weeks/5 months for 3-dose) and 'repeat dose if administered too soon' validity logic not represented; doses before minimum age 9 are not excluded from counts.
HPV: 'No additional dose recommended' after completion of any-valency series not represented beyond count logic.
HPV special situation: history of sexual abuse or assault -> start at age 9 (needs abuse history; uncomputable) not encoded as a rule.
HPV: pregnancy deferral ('not recommended until after pregnancy'), no pregnancy test needed, no intervention if vaccinated while pregnant - not represented.

Influenza: ages 6 months-8 years need 2 doses (>=4 weeks apart) if fewer than 2 doses before July 1, 2024 or history unknown, otherwise 1 dose - depends on prior dose history and sub-year ages; not encoded.
Influenza: calendar-year window approximates the influenza season; 2024-25 and 2025-26 season-specific ACIP recommendations (external references) not captured.
Influenza: product choice (IIV3, LAIV3 min age 2, RIV3 min age 18; HD-IIV3/aIIV3 acceptable for age-18 solid organ transplant recipients on immunosuppression) not represented.

Influenza: close contacts of severely immunosuppressed persons should not receive LAIV3 (7-day contact avoidance) - contraindication/exposure-dependent, not represented. Egg allergy note: any vaccine acceptable.
MMR: doses given before 12 months (e.g., travel dose at 6-11 months) should not count toward the series; grammar cannot exclude birth-relative early doses.
MMR: minimum intervals (4 weeks; 3 months between MMRV doses) and MMRV maximum age 12 years not represented; preference for separate MMR+varicella for dose 1 at 12-47 months not represented.
MMR: international travel acceleration (infants 6-11 months 1 dose before departure; age 12 months+ 2 doses before departure) needs travel history - uncomputable, not encoded.
MMR: mumps outbreak 3rd dose guidance (external reference) not represented.
MMR: evidence of immunity (serology/history) exclusions are not stated in this section and were not added.
Age 18 upper bound for influenza and MMR rules is taken from the schedule title ('for Ages 18 Years or Younger').
